text: Isabel Allende's The House of the Spirits was challenged on the tenth grade reading list at La Costa Canyon High School in Encinitas, Calif., in 1999 because the book allegedly “defames” the Catholic faith and contains “pornographic passages.” In 2000 it was retained on summer reading lists for honors high school students at the Fairfield-Suisun Unified School District, Calif., despite objections that it was “immoral and sexually depraved.” In 2003 it was challenged but retained in advanced English classes in Modesto, Calif.; the seven-member Modesto City School Board said administrators should give parents more information about the books their children read. In 2013 it was challenged in the Watauga County, N.C. High School curriculum because of its graphic nature, and after a five-month process was fully retained at a third and final appeal hearing.
meta_description: The House of the Spirits by Isabel Allende: challenged in California schools in 1999, 2000 and 2003 and in North Carolina in 2013; retained.
